doc.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022

chapter: The jazz business and hard bop
title: A patron for the Cookers and Slide Hampton's Messengers charts
summary: Asked whether he would focus on the Cookers with a patron, Weiss says the pandemic has already made that so, and describes discovering Slide Hampton's unrecorded sextet charts for Art Blakey that he is transcribing.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Fresh, okay. Fresh is good. In your career, you’ve, it seems to be a constant balancing and juggling of tasks that you’ve learned you can do, and I wonder if some patron happened to drop in the scene and said, “I’m going to finance” let’s say, “the Cookers for © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

a year. That’s all I want you to do, this group is so important I’m going to finance the whole thing for a solid year.” Do you think you would have trouble doing that and giving up all the other things that you do?

Well I mean as I kind of said, the question has a different meaning now, interestingly. (a) like I said, the pandemic has kind of eliminated everything else. I mean I’ve been doing some things at home, I’ve known about some of this music before but I’ve discovered some things. There’s an interesting period, I mean this is like the historical part of me which is fun, and this is the kind of thing where if things were normal I’d be like okay let me get this somewhere and try it. But apparently, I mean I sort of knew some of this, I know it better now. Apparently in 1967 Art Blakey hired Slide Hampton for the Messengers and to be the musical director. And Slide wrote a bunch of music, like sextet charts. And they’re great. And they’ve never been officially recorded. You can see some bootlegs of it. There’s a recording from RCA Studios, George Wein’s birthday party where Art Blakey’s band plays a set and they’re in RCA Studios so they pressed “record” and it’s just sitting there, nobody knows about it. But I got, in my capacity of other work I got to hear it and it’s all Slide Hampton charts. And there’s videos from 1968 and Slide’s not even in the band, but they’re playing all of Slide’s material. And they’re sextet charts and I’m enamored with sextet charts. I cut my teeth on learning how to write those Wayne Shorter sextet charts and all that stuff. And they’re great. And I’ve been transcribing them and I’ll do them eventually but that can wait a year to do this. I mean the timing is now. It feels like I’m almost just focusing on the Cookers now you know. Because when things are a little uncertain, things are not opening up, I mean honestly to give the David Weiss Sextet a gig now, when things are like you know you’re not sure if people are coming out or whatever. I think I’m a tough sell right now. You know when things are more opened up and things are functioning normally and everybody has full schedules you know, but right now I’m focusing on the Cookers. And also I mean two years off — well it hasn’t been two years off — a year off shows you anything you know nobody’s a baby you know. I don’t want to be like strike while the iron’s hot but you know let’s play while everybody is — yeah, I’ll take it. And that can do it if there’s an urgency, I don’t know maybe I’m the one that’s going to get hit by a bus and be the one. I wouldn’t call it [inaudible] but there is a sense there that you know, hey, we’re not going to do this for another ten years.
